scenes.narration: Nvidia builds the fastest AI math chips on Earth, and they still spend most of the day waiting. Not for electricity, and not for code, but for memory.
Imagine ten thousand chefs trapped behind one tiny doorway. Flat memory chips sit too far away on the circuit board, burning power just moving numbers back and forth.
In 2013, SK Hynix tried a radical fix: shave memory silicon paper-thin, stack twelve layers into a vertical tower, and drill thousands of microscopic elevators straight through.
Benchmarks proved it could beat traditional CPU setups by up to twelve point nine times. By 2025, AI data centers bought out the world's supply, triggering a global memory shortage.
But here is the catch: HBM towers are custom-bonded to each chip a year in advance. What made SK Hynix AI's kingmaker also locks it to a single boom. Full story on Tradeoff Layer.
